blogs.title: Propensity or Possession? Navigating the Line Between Rule 404(b) and Intrinsic Evidence
blogs.description: This post analyzes the Eighth Circuit's ruling that testimony regarding a defendant's prior possession of a specific firearm is intrinsic evidence of ownership and control rather than prohibited propensity evidence under Federal Rule of Evidence 404(b). It explores the practical implications for the government's burden of proof in felon-in-possession cases and the narrow distinction between showing a 'pattern of behavior' versus establishing a 'link to a weapon.'

blogs.title: Timing the Warning: Limiting Instructions and the Confrontation Clause
blogs.description: An examination of the court's decision regarding the timing of limiting instructions when hearsay is introduced at trial. This post discusses the tension between the immediate need to prevent jury prejudice and the court's discretion to provide a single instruction at the close of trial, specifically in cases where the Confrontation Clause is eventually satisfied by the witness's testimony.

blogs.title: The 'Greater Offense Level' Tug-of-War: USSG Enhancements and § 3553(a) Reasonableness
blogs.description: This post delves into the sentencing mechanics of United States v. Cutbank, specifically the application of USSG § 2K2.1(b)(6)(B) and the 'greater offense level' rule. It analyzes the legal conflict between the rigid application of sentencing enhancements and the statutory mandate under 18 U.S.C. § 3553(a) that a sentence be 'sufficient, but not greater than necessary,' questioning when a guidelines-based sentence becomes substantively unreasonable.
